subject: Greenline: request for access logs, IR timeline, and post-incident artifacts
messages:
From: Alex Bryant <abryant@greenline.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Suspicious API activity — initial notification and artifacts

Hi team,

We observed anomalous API usage against our account that appears to have used a short-lived key tied to an internal service account. The traffic pattern looks like a credential replay: multiple callers from two distinct IP ranges calling a high-privilege endpoint between 02:04–02:18 UTC.

Attached is a slice of the event stream (greenline_event_log_1011.json) and a short list of affected resource IDs. We are running an internal investigation and need Redwood to:

- Confirm whether the requests originated inside Redwood infrastructure or via a Redwood-issued credential.
- Share a 24-hour window of Cloud API access logs and any associated token issuance or rotation events for the service account id: svc-greenline-sync.
- Provide your incident response point-of-contact and an estimated timeline for preliminary findings.

This is time-sensitive for our SOC 2 evidence collection. Can you confirm receipt and a first ETA by EOD PST?

Thanks,
Alex Bryant
Director, Security Operations
Greenline Financial

---

On Sun, 11 Oct 2026 at 09:03 -0700, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Alex Bryant <abryant@greenline.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious API activity — initial notification and artifacts

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the log slice. We’ve received the file and started a triage. Quick confirmations:

- We are treating this as a potential credential exposure.
- Point-of-contact for this incident will be Aditya Rao (for forensic collection) and myself (customer communication / SOC 2 evidence).

Aditya — can you validate whether the svc-greenline-sync token was issued by our hosted token service and share the issuance records + token id hash if available? Also prepare CloudTrail (24h), our edge access logs, and any node-level container logs for the implicated timeframe.

Alex, we will aim to deliver a preliminary timeline and the requested artifacts by tomorrow 17:00 PST. We will not share full raw logs in this thread; we’ll provide secure links.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Security Lead, Redwood Inference

---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, Alex Bryant <abryant@greenline.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious API activity — initial notification and artifacts

Updating with what I have so far and the immediate asks we can fulfill: 

Summary of checks completed (prelim):
- Token service audit: found an issuance event for a token matching svc-greenline-sync on 2026-10-11T02:02:15Z. Token id (redacted) ends with -a3f.
- Edge proxy logs: multiple inbound requests from two IP ranges that do not match Greenline-managed IPs; request signatures matched the issued token.
- No anomalous container restarts observed in the same window.

What we will provide by 2026-10-12 16:00 UTC (delivery plan):
- Redacted CloudTrail for 2026-10-10 00:00 UTC through 2026-10-11 23:59 UTC (sensitive fields masked).
- Edge access logs for the implicated endpoints (CSV slice) and the token issuance audit trail (token id hash only).
- A short preliminary timeline (PDF) capturing detection, mitigation steps we took (rotated keys, revoked active sessions), and recommended next steps. (See attached prelim_kv_snapshot.txt as a short artifact placeholder.)

Actions already taken:
- Rotated the svc-greenline-sync credential and revoked active sessions tied to the token id.
- Throttled the affected endpoints for all inbound Greenline-origin traffic pending validation (we will avoid broad rate limits to prevent production impact).

Requests back to Greenline:
1) Please confirm whether any internal Greenline rotation or deploys occurred 02:00–03:00 UTC that could have exposed a token.
2) If you have a CI/CD log or Secrets Manager rotation event, share the ticket id or link. That will speed correlation.

We will publish artifacts to a secure Drive folder and send you links via the customer portal (not in-line).

- Aditya Rao
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Bryant <abryant@greenline.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Suspicious API activity — initial notification and artifacts

Alex — thanks for collaborating on this. We've uploaded the preliminary artifacts and timeline to a secure folder and opened a Jira ticket (GL-4721) for the coordinated postmortem. Link below.

Deliverables (links attached):
- Preliminary IR timeline (redwood_ir_timeline_draft.pdf) — high level chronology and mitigation actions.
- Cloud audit slice (redacted) and edge log CSV.
- Token issuance audit (hashed ids only) and revocation events.

Next steps we propose:
- Joint war room war to finalize root cause (optional) — propose Tue 2026-10-13 08:00 PST.
- Map artifacts to SOC 2 control objectives and provide a SIG/CAIQ matrix that identifies evidence locations (we can provide this by 2026-10-15).
- If Greenline wants a formal postmortem write-up suitable for vendor risk teams, we will prepare a redacted postmortem for distribution.

Alex replied: "Appreciate the rapid response. Please include the CAIQ/SIG mapping in the artifact bundle — our auditors will expect control IDs tied to each log set. We’ll confirm the war room slot after checking internal calendars"

Attachments (shared via secure link): greenline_event_log_1011.json, prelim_kv_snapshot.txt, redwood_ir_timeline_draft.pdf

--
Evelyn Hart
Incident Response Program Manager
Redwood Inference
